The '''2026 New York gubernatorial election''' is scheduled to take place on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of New York]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Kathy Hochul]] is running for re-election to a second full term.<ref name="HochulRunning">{{Cite web |last=Parsnow |first=Luke |date=July 2, 2024 |title=Hochul says she's running for another term as New York governor in 2026 |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/central-ny/politics/2024/07/02/hochul-says-she-s-running-for-another-term-as-governor-in-2026 |access-date=August 20, 2024 |website=[[Spectrum News]] |language=en |archive-date=July 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240708215410/https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/central-ny/politics/2024/07/02/hochul-says-she-s-running-for-another-term-as-governor-in-2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Primary elections]] took place on June 23, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 9, 2025|title=2026 State Primary Election Dates|url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260423040741/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-date=April 23, 2026|access-date=August 5, 2025|website=[[National Conference of State Legislatures|NCSL]]}}</ref> The gubernatorial candidates selected their running mates, instead of having separate primaries.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cuza|first=Bobby|date=May 8, 2025|title=State lawmakers eliminate lieutenant governor primary|url=https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/politics/2025/05/09/albany-lawmakers-eliminate-lieutenant-governor-primary?cid=share_clip|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260105102847/https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/politics/2025/05/09/albany-lawmakers-eliminate-lieutenant-governor-primary?cid=share_clip|archive-date=January 5, 2026|website=[[Spectrum News]]}}</ref> 

Hochul will face Nassau County executive [[Bruce Blakeman]], the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] and [[Conservative Party of New York State|Conservative]] nominee, in the general election. After U.S. representative [[Elise Stefanik]] withdrew from the Republican primary in December 2025, Blakeman was endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]].<ref name="te">{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/12/20/trump-new-york-governor-endorsement-bruce-blakeman-00702013|title=Trump endorses in New York governor race the day after Stefanik drops out|date=December 20, 2025|website=POLITICO}}</ref> Republicans have not won a statewide election in New York since [[George Pataki]] was re-elected governor in [[2002 New York gubernatorial election|2002]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://abc7ny.com/post/new-york-rep-elise-stefanik-announce-run-governor-soon-friday/18122558/|title=Rep. Elise Stefanik to announce run for New York governor as soon as Friday|date=November 6, 2025|website=ABC7 New York}}</ref>

==Background==
Governor [[Kathy Hochul]] took office on August 24, 2021, upon the resignation of her predecessor, [[Andrew Cuomo]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/24/nyregion/kathy-hochul-governor-ny.html|title=Hochul Is Sworn In: 'I Want People to Believe in Their Government Again'|first=Luis|last=Ferré-Sadurní|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=August 24, 2021}}</ref> Hochul was elected to a full term in [[2022 New York gubernatorial election|2022]] with 53.1% of the vote in the closest New York gubernatorial election since [[1994 New York gubernatorial election|1994]].<ref name="results">{{cite web |title=2022 General Election Governor and Lt. Governor Results |url=https://elections.ny.gov/2022-general-election-governor-and-lt-governor-results |website=[[New York State Board of Elections]]|date=November 8, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.timesunion.com/state/article/Zeldin-concede-17571499.php|title=Zeldin concedes to Hochul in closest governor's race since 1994|first=Brendan J.|last=Lyons|date=November 9, 2022|website=Times Union}}</ref>

==Democratic primary==
Due to low approval ratings, poor Democratic performances in the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|2022 midterm elections]] in [[2022 New York state elections|New York]], and controversies surrounding her administration, Hochul was considered vulnerable to a primary challenge in 2026.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Reisman |first=Nick |date=September 5, 2024 |title=Hochul's headwinds become tougher with indictment of alleged foreign agent |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2024/09/05/linda-sun-arrest-hochul-approval-00177430?nname=new-york-playbook&nid=0000014f-1646-d88f-a1cf-5f46b74f0000&nrid=7fbb50ed-ea1a-4aff-a106-d6b8cc25c14a&nlid=630317 |work=[[Politico]]}}</ref> 

On June 2, 2025, following months of reports about a strained relationship with the governor's office, [[Antonio Delgado]] launched his campaign for the Democratic nomination.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Mays |first=Jeffery C. |date=June 2, 2025 |title=Antonio Delgado, Hochul's No. 2, Will Challenge Her in Governor's Race |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/02/nyregion/antonio-delgado-governor-hochul.html |access-date=June 2, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> On February 4, 2026, he announced nurse, union organizer, and socialist activist [[India Walton]] as his running mate.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/capital-region/politics/2026/02/04/antonio-delgado-governor-election-running-mate|title=Delgado picks India Walton as running mate in governor's race|date=February 4, 2026|website=spectrumlocalnews.com}}</ref> 

Despite early perceptions of vulnerability to a left-wing challenge, Hochul was endorsed in February 2026 by [[Zohran Mamdani]] and [[Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]], both prominent members of the [[New York City Democratic Socialists of America]]. ''[[Politico]]'' noted that the endorsements "all but crowd out her little-known primary challenger, (Antonio) Delgado," while Democratic strategist Trip Yang called Hochul "the comeback player of the year."<ref name="embrace">{{cite web |title=Why the left decided to embrace, and not fight, Kathy Hochul |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/06/why-the-left-decided-to-embrace-and-not-fight-kathy-hochul-00769785 |website=[[Politico]] |access-date=2026-02-08 |language=en |date=2026-02-06}}</ref> She was soon endorsed by the [[New York State Democratic Party|New York Democratic Party]] after securing 85% of support from party members at the state convention,<ref>{{cite web |title=Hochul projects 'strength' as she resoundingly wins Democratic backing for a new term |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/06/hochul-projects-strength-as-she-resoundingly-wins-democratic-backing-for-a-new-term-00769561 |website=POLITICO |access-date=2026-02-13 |language=en |date=2026-02-06}}</ref> and Delgado ended his campaign on February 10, 2026, citing a lack of a viable path forward.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Sterne |first1=Peter |last2=Lewis |first2=Rebecca |date=February 10, 2026 |title=Antonio Delgado ends his campaign for governor |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/02/antonio-delgado-ends-his-campaign-governor/411320/ |access-date=2026-02-10 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref>

==Republican primary==
U.S. representative [[Elise Stefanik]] was considered a potential gubernatorial candidate throughout 2025. She formally announced her candidacy on November 7, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rep. Elise Stefanik announces run for New York governor, challenging Kathy Hochul in 2026 election - CBS New York |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/elise-stefanik-running-for-new-york-governor/ |website=CBS |access-date=November 7, 2025 |date=November 7, 2025}}</ref> A July 2025 Siena poll showed Stefanik leading two other potential Republican gubernatorial candidates, U.S. representative [[Mike Lawler]] and Nassau County executive [[Bruce Blakeman]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/central-ny/politics/2025/06/30/poll--stefanik-leads-potential-gop-field-for-n-y--governor|title=Poll: Stefanik leads potential GOP field for N.Y. governor; Hochul leads all 3|website=spectrumlocalnews.com|last=Parsnow|first=Luke}}</ref> In May 2025, President [[Donald Trump]] endorsed Lawler and Blakeman for re-election to their current posts "in a not-so-subtle attempt to clear the field for upstate Congresswoman Elise Stefanik to get the GOP nomination".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/trump-bruce-blakeman-mike-lawler-endorsements/|title=Ahead of N.Y. governor's race, President Trump's endorsements send "loud message" |last=Kramer|first=Marcia|date=May 7, 2025|website=www.cbsnews.com}}</ref> On July 23, 2025, Mike Lawler announced that he would run for re-election to Congress.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Anderson |first1=Renee |last2=Kramer |first2=Marcia |last3=Woodall |first3=Hunter |date=July 23, 2025 |title=Mike Lawler to sit out New York governor's race and run for reelection in House district |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/mike-lawler-reelection-new-york-governor-race-elise-stefanik-republicans/ |access-date=July 30, 2025 |website=[[CBS News]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Bruce Blakeman was re-elected to the post of Nassau County executive by a double-digit margin in November 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gothamist.com/news/blakeman-reelected-as-nassau-county-exec-and-gop-hopes-for-a-bulwark-against-mamdani|title=Blakeman reelected as Nassau County exec and GOP hopes for a bulwark against Mamdani|first=Jimmy|last=Vielkind|date=November 5, 2025|website=Gothamist}}</ref> When asked about Blakeman's potential gubernatorial candidacy, Trump stated that Blakeman and Stefanik were "both great people".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://abcnews.com/Politics/county-gop-leader-bruce-blakeman-announces-run-new/story?id=128244979|title=County GOP leader Bruce Blakeman announces run for New York governor, taking on fellow Trump ally Elise Stefanik|first=Oren|last=Oppenheim|website=ABC News|date=December 9, 2025}}</ref> On December 9, 2025, Blakeman launched his campaign for the 2026 Republican gubernatorial nomination.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bruce Blakeman launches bid for New York governor|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/video/bruce-blakeman-launches-bid-for-new-york-governor/ |access-date=December 9, 2025 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref> According to ''[[The New York Times]]'', Trump's decision to remain neutral and not to attempt to clear the field for Stefanik "sent shock waves through Republican circles".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/10/nyregion/blakeman-trump-stefanik.html|title=Trump Didn't Clear a Path for Stefanik in the N.Y. Governor's Race|first=Grace|last=Ashford|work=The New York Times |date=December 10, 2025|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref> On December 19, Stefanik announced she was withdrawing her candidacy.<ref name="sq">{{Cite web |last=Jacobs |first=Ben |date=December 19, 2025 |title=Stefanik Quits Governor's Race, Will Not Run for Reelection |url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/elise-stefanik-new-york-governor-interview.html |access-date=December 19, 2025 |website=Intelligencer |language=en}}</ref> President Trump endorsed Blakeman's candidacy on December 20.<ref name="te"/>

In February 2026, Libertarian nominee Larry Sharpe announced his intention to petition his way onto the Republican primary ballot.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/02/state-gop-formally-designates-blakeman-nominee-governor/411361/|title=State GOP formally designates Blakeman as nominee for governor|first=Rebecca C.|last=Lewis|date=February 11, 2026|website=City & State NY}}</ref>

==Conservative convention==
The [[New York State Conservative Party]] held its annual conference and nominating convention in Albany in February 2026, officially endorsing Blakeman for governor. Because New York utilizes a fusion voting system, Blakeman accepted the third-party ballot line to run concurrently on both the Republican and Conservative lines.<ref name="ConservativeLine">{{cite web |title=Bruce Blakeman receives nomination for governor from NY State Conservative Party |url=https://longisland.news12.com/bruce-blakeman-receives-nomination-for-governor-from-ny-state-conservative-party |website=News 12 |access-date=2026-02-15}}</ref>
===Candidates===
====Nominee====
*[[Bruce Blakeman]], [[Nassau County Executive|Nassau County executive]] (2021–present)<ref name="ConservativeLine"/>
**Running mate: Todd Hood, [[Madison County, New York|Madison County]] sheriff (2018–present)<ref name="HoodLtGov"/>

==Working Families convention==
The [[Working Families Party|New York Working Families Party]] declined to nominate Hochul or Delgado, instead opting for a "placeholder candidate" to appear on their ballot line. The party has stated that the placeholder candidate will later be replaced by the Democratic nominee.<ref name="Placeholder"/> A convention attendee told ''[[City & State]]'' that Delgado won 41% of the weighted party committee vote to Hochul's 3%, while "placeholder candidate" won 56% of the vote. State party leaders Jasmine Gripper and [[Ana María Archila]] disputed the claim, but did not share the exact vote totals.<ref name="Placeholder"/>

On August 21, the Working Families Party nominated Hochul and Adams.<ref name="WFPLine"/>
===Candidates===
====Nominee====
*[[Kathy Hochul]], [[governor of New York]] (2021–present)<ref name="WFPLine">{{Cite web |last1=Mahoney |first1=Bill |date=2026-08-21 |url=https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2026/08/working-families-party-gives-its-ballot-line-to-hochul-01045637 |title=Working Families Party gives its ballot line to Hochul |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=Politico |language=en-US}}</ref>
**Running mate: [[Adrienne Adams (politician)|Adrienne Adams]], former speaker of the [[New York City Council]] (2022–2025) from the [[New York City's 28th City Council district|28th district]] (2017–2025) and candidate for [[mayor of New York City]] in [[2025 New York City mayoral election|2025]]<ref name="WFPLine"/>
 
== Independents and other parties ==
The [[New York State Board of Elections]] rejected all petitions for non-qualified party ballot access in May 2026.<ref name="BOEDisqualification">{{cite web |title=2026 General Prima Facie and Hearing Report |url=https://elections.ny.gov/2026-general-prima-facie-and-hearing-report |website=New York State Board of Elections |date=June 4, 2026 |access-date=June 26, 2026}}</ref>
